details.publicNotes:
Common woodplucks are small, plump fey, and they don't look like much of a threat, though thanks to the power of their imaginations, they can be more dangerous than they look to fledgling adventurers who decide to pick a fight with them.

Woodplucks tend to make their homes in large communities in forests. They subtly alter the color and texture of their bodies to match the trees they live around. Teamwork is prized in woodpluck culture. Singing is also a cultural touchstone, as it is one of the best ways to align the thoughts of a group together. The sprouts of a group of singing woodplucks dance in unison, portraying the various events and emotions their voices describe.

Despite the difficulty woodplucks have with hiding their thoughts, they love pulling pranks and practical jokes. It's considered a sign of respect among woodplucks to allow tricks to play out even when you see them ahead of time. It's easy to see a joke coming when the comedian has a giggling flower on their head, but outsiders are well advised to play along to avoid causing offense.

Woodplucks are plump fey creatures with a single arm protruding from their torsos. Their eager imaginations manifest in physical form through a small plant sprout embedded in each individual's head, which grows and shapes itself into whatever the host woodpluck is thinking about at the time. When a woodpluck sleeps, their sprout's roots dig into their mind and grow out into the most vivid scenes of their dreams.

Woodplucks can gather in choruses to work together, and when their imagination grows, they can become powerful elders.

Take This, It's Dangerous to go Alone!

Woodplucks are generous to a fault, always eager to share the fruits of their imaginations with outsiders. In fact, some woodplucks consider it impolite to leave an interaction with a non-woodpluck without offering them some sort of gift, such as a weapon or useful tool. Unfortunately, woodplucks don't seem fully aware that their gifts only last as long as their attention does. When the woodpluck cultivates a new item, the recipient of their "gift" might find that it dissolves in their hand at the most inconvenient time.

Suggested Monster Parts

Monster Parts 5/12/22 gp

Eligible Refinements weapons (piercing, slashing), armor (medium), skill items (Acrobatics, Crafting, Deception, Diplomacy, Nature, Performance, Stealth)

Eligible Imbued Properties bane, charisma, constitution, dexterity, energy resistant (vitality), mind, mind shield, sensory (low-light vision), tangle shield, throwing, wild, wisdom, wood

description.value: The woodpluck merges their body into an adjacent tree. While merged, they can't take any actions that require their body (including Cultivate Imagination), but they can still use their mind and senses as normal while merged. They can exit the tree into any space adjacent to the tree as a two-action activity, ending the effect.
When a woodpluck wields a melee weapon they created with Cultivate Imagination, the weapon produces splinters on impact, dealing an additional 1d4 piercing damage.

The woodpluck sings a powerful song, and their sprout dances along with them. The woodpluck chooses up to four creatures within 30 feet, which must each attempt a @Check[will|dc:18] save.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinated} for 1 round.

Critical Failure The creature is fascinated and stunned for 1 round.

The woodpluck imagines a common level 0 non-magical weapon, shield, piece of adventuring gear, or simple tool of no more than 1 Bulk, which then grows on their head. The cultivated item is made entirely from wood and other plant matter, but otherwise functions as the base item. The woodpluck can then Interact to grab the item. The most common weapons imagined by woodplucks are listed in their Strikes above. Cultivating an item in this way causes any items previously created by the woodpluck's imagination to break down into ordinary plant matter.
